solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something modelled on The Last of the Mohicans?

definitions.text: Something modelled on The Last of the Mohicans?

blocks.note: reads as something copied from an original, but footwear is shaped on a model foot
a novel on the surface; a last is a shoemaker's wooden foot form, so this is the Mohicans' own last

explanation.surface: A question about what was inspired by Fenimore Cooper's frontier novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the wooden foot shape a shoemaker builds a shoe on, so a shoe shaped on the Mohicans' last is their soft leather slipper. The book title is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is the soft leather shoe of North American peoples such as the Mohicans, so it was made on their last.

clue.text: A single person is included in text

indicators.note: something included in a thing is inside it, so the first piece sits inside the second

blocks.note: a = one = I
an SMS is a text message, split around the I

explanation.surface: A remark that a lone person appears somewhere in a written passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A single person' reads as one unit, but the wordplay borrows 'A' as I, and it also stays part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman, so it stands for a single person.

clue.text: Show inclination for hypocrisy

blocks.note: to tilt or slope, as a ship leans over
insincere, pious talk

explanation.surface: Someone showing a taste for hypocrisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' reads as a preference, but it means a physical slant.
explanation.definitionFit: To cant is to lean or tilt, and cant is also hollow, hypocritical talk.

clue.text: Over period, modify highly informative device

indicators.note: one thing over another covers it

blocks.note: to alter is to modify
a period of time, sitting in the middle of the verb

explanation.surface: An instruction to change a device over a period so it tells you more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly informative' is a joke: the device informs you how high you are.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter tells a pilot the altitude, so it gives information about height.

clue.text: During time for learning at home, showing proficiency endlessly

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the war'
a school or university term
to be in = to be at home
doing something ably shows skill

explanation.surface: A student at home during term, getting better and better without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like a deletion instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that goes on interminably never seems to end.

clue.text: Work of art, say, outside university

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it

blocks.note: to state is to say
U = university, placed within the verb

explanation.surface: A sculpture, perhaps, standing outside a university building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the usual signal that an example follows, but it is the verb STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a statue is a sculpted figure, a classic kind of work of art.

clue.text: Riding (not South) behind two others

blocks.note: Yorkshire was once split into three Ridings, North, East and West; the name comes from Old Norse for a one-in-three part
the position of a runner with two ahead

explanation.surface: A rider trailing two others in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A Riding was one of the historic divisions of Yorkshire, an English county. '(Not South)' is there because there was no South Riding, and it keeps the clue true.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fractions of order: each Riding was one of three parts of the county, and a runner behind two others finishes in that place.

clue.text: Chance it in rearrangement as practical expert

indicators.note: things in rearrangement are being put in a new order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Advice to take a gamble on a reshuffle and pose as a skilled hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of 'Chance it in' belongs to the fodder, while the 'in' of 'in rearrangement' is part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a technician is someone skilled in the practical, hands-on side of a trade.

clue.text: Seasonal flower I left in wind

indicators.note: 'in' places something inside

blocks.note: an easterly is a wind from the east
I stays I
L = left, joining I inside the wind

explanation.surface: A flower of the season, battered by a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasonal' points at Easter, the festival at which white lilies decorate churches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Easter lily is a white trumpet lily associated with the Easter season, hence seasonal.

clue.text: Godliness in court, within reason

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court, set inside reason
sanity = reason, a sound mind

explanation.surface: Holiness found in a courtroom, within reasonable limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within reason' is a stock phrase meaning 'in moderation', which hides that 'reason' is SANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sanctity is the state of being holy, which is godliness.

clue.text: Talk about not finishing — throwing up contest

indicators.note: a word not finishing stops short, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a seven-letter verb for talking something over, ending in a double S; its final letter is lost

explanation.surface: Someone who can't finish talking about a vomiting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing up' suggests being sick, but here it means hurling the disc up into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is an athletic event in which a heavy disc is thrown up and away.

clue.text: Head off rebel advancing incrementally

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a revolutionary is a rebel; its first letter R is taken off

explanation.surface: An order to intercept a rebel who is creeping forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as 'intercept', but it tells you to remove the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolutionary change advances gradually, step by step, rather than by revolution.

clue.text: With such lack of foresight, I’m in front of state capital

indicators.note: something in front of another comes first

blocks.note: I'm, with the apostrophe dropped
Providence is the capital of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A careless person boasting of being ahead of the state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue needs the solver to name a specific US state capital; Providence, Rhode Island, is the one that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvidence is failure to provide for the future, which comes from a lack of foresight.

clue.text: Police raid disrupted publication

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A police raid that stopped a newspaper from coming out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a plausible news story, so 'disrupted' reads as its verb rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a periodical is a magazine or journal published at regular intervals.

clue.text: Price often adjusted — that’s achievable in practice

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who keeps tweaking prices, claiming the right figure can be found by trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the proverb 'practice makes perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the proverb says practice makes perfect, so perfection is what practice achieves.

clue.text: What happened repeatedly in 1770

blocks.note: a plain description of an occurrence
write 1770 out as seventeen seventy: the same five letters sit inside each word, just after the S

explanation.surface: A question about what happened again and again in the year 1770.
explanation.walkthrough: The date tempts you to recall history, such as Cook reaching Australia, but the trick is to write the number in words: sEVENTeen sEVENTy.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence is a plain synonym for what happened, and the five letters appear once in each word of 'seventeen seventy'.

clue.text: After 1:50, serving American in pub is unjustifiable

indicators.note: 'in' places something inside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the Roman numeral fifty
a local is one's nearby pub
a GI is an American serviceman, set inside the pub

explanation.surface: Staying in the pub serving an American after ten to two is indefensible.
explanation.walkthrough: '1:50' looks like a time of day, but you read it as the Roman numerals 1 and 50.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an illogical position has no sound reasoning, so it cannot be justified.

clue.text: Get excited and extend hand?

blocks.note: a slang phrase for going wild
growers call a cluster of this fruit a hand, so a growing hand adds more of them

explanation.surface: Someone getting excited and holding out a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second sense: a hand is the growers' word for a cluster of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go bananas is slang for becoming wildly excited.

clue.text: Within stronghold, holding soldier who betrays others?

definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause standing for 'one who betrays others'

indicators.note: something holding another has it inside

blocks.note: in = within
a fort is a stronghold
a man is a private soldier, held inside the stronghold

explanation.surface: A soldier holed up in a fortress who turns traitor on his comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' reads as the container instruction, but it gives IN, and 'holding' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: An informant passes on information about others to the authorities, betraying them.

clue.text: Boxer’s beginning with crude left in fight

indicators.note: 'beginning' is the start of a word, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of boxer
raw = crude, unrefined
L = left

explanation.surface: A boxer starting a bout with a crude left hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link here, not a container signal: the pieces just run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brawl is a noisy, disorderly fight.

clue.text: Wrongly claimed way to use digit that separates two of them

indicators.note: something done wrongly is done amiss, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: anagram of the seven letters
you point with a finger, a digit

explanation.surface: Someone claiming, wrongly, the right way to use a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digit' means a finger in the wordplay, then 'them' in the definition switches it to numerical digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal point sits between two digits, separating whole numbers from fractions.

clue.text: Part of America with ocean on East

indicators.note: one thing on another is added to it

blocks.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
E = east

explanation.surface: A region of America with the ocean on its east side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: Maine is the US state on the Atlantic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Maine is one of the United States, the northeasternmost, so a part of America.

clue.text: Former politician providing cover for head, reportedly

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as people say it, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a wig covers the head

explanation.surface: An old politician who is said to have worn a hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were a British political party of the 17th to 19th centuries, which is why the politician is 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Whig was a member of the old British party that became the Liberals, long gone now.

clue.text: React angrily — gratuities raised

indicators.note: something raised is lifted up, and in a down entry a word read upwards is reversed

blocks.note: tips are gratuities

explanation.surface: Someone furious that the tips have been increased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reads as 'increased', but in a down entry it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit is to show fury, as an angry cat does.

clue.text: Disaster is repeated following first couple of crashes

indicators.note: 'repeated' means said again, so the word 'is' is used twice
'following' means coming after
a couple is two, so the first two letters are taken

blocks.note: the first two letters of crashes
IS stays IS
IS again

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes again after a pair of crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is repeated' reads as part of the story, but it simply means write IS twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a crisis is a time of severe difficulty, close to disaster.

clue.text: Exploited people bound to be found in lending business

blocks.note: pawns are people used by others
a hop is a bound, a jump

explanation.surface: Exploited people who are sure to end up at a moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'certain' in the surface; the wordplay wants the leap, HOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnshop lends money against goods left as security.

clue.text: Journal that is enlightening for insiders

blocks.note: a famous British medical journal
a tall, narrow pointed window that lets light in for people inside a church

explanation.surface: A publication that informs those in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enlightening' suggests informing, which is what a journal does; the second sense is literal light, through a pointed Gothic window.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancet is a medical journal, and a lancet window lights a church interior.

clue.text: Ability to see positive response in crew

indicators.note: 'in' places something inside

blocks.note: yes is a positive answer, set inside the crew
an eight is a rowing crew of eight

explanation.surface: Checking whether a crew has the vision needed.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing boat rowed by eight oarsmen, and by extension its crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: eyesight is the faculty of vision, the ability to see.
